headline: Nothing cancels CMF phone due to high RAM prices
summary: The CMF phone successor won't launch this year. RAM prices are unsustainable.
details: Nothing's co-founder Akis Evangelidis announced that a follow-up to the CMF Phone 2 Pro won't be coming this year. The reason is due to high RAM prices, making it impossible to build a phone 'at a price that makes sense.'

Nothing CEO Carl Pei also mentioned that memory costs doubled between when they decided to build the Phone 4A and when it launched, and have doubled again since. Memory is now the most expensive component in a smartphone.

Despite cancelling the CMF phone, Evangelidis added that CMF still has 'several new products launching as well as some entirely new categories.' The smartphone launch season at Nothing 'isn't over yet.'

headline_marked: 7,000 [[Langflow servers under attack]] via CVE-2026-5027 exploit
headline: 7,000 Langflow servers under attack via CVE-2026-5027 exploit
summary: Langflow servers are being exploited via CVE-2026-5027, a path traversal vulnerability. Over 7,000 instances are exposed online.
details: Langflow, a popular AI agent framework, has over 7,000 servers exposed online and is currently under attack. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-5027, is a path traversal in the POST /api/v2/files endpoint.

The vulnerability allows an attacker to write files anywhere on the system, including dropping a cron job in /etc/cron.d/ to gain a shell. This exploit does not require any credentials if Langflow is configured with auto-login enabled, which is the default configuration.

CVE-2026-5027 has a CVSS score of 8.8 and was patched in version 1.9.0, released on April 15. However, attacks started in June, and VulnCheck added CVE-2026-5027 to its exploited-vulnerabilities list on June 8.

LangGraph and LangChain have also been found to have vulnerabilities, including SQL injection and path traversal issues, which can lead to remote code execution. These frameworks have been widely deployed and have become production infrastructure quickly, but security measures have not kept pace.

The fixes for LangGraph are version bumps: langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite to 3.0.1, langgraph to 1.0.10, and langgraph-checkpoint-redis to 1.0.2. There has been no confirmed exploitation in the wild yet, but a working proof-of-concept is public.
